{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror
","path":"scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"}

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror
","path":"scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"}

blocks.text:
Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

messages.preview: `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` bypasses the wrapper. Patching the selftest's REAL_GIT resolution:

blocks.text:
- `command -v git` → the guard wrapper (PATH-prepended by the harness).
- `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` (system default PATH) — exactly what I need for the selftest's REAL_GIT.

This is also a noteworthy environment gotcha for the memory: this runner prepends a `git-push-guard-bin` wrapper to PATH; any script that resolves a "real" tool via `command -v` gets the wrapper. (`command -v -p` bypasses it.)

Now fix the selftest: replace `REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"` with a resolution that skips wrappers:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || command -v git)"
```

On macOS (selftest is runnable locally too) `command -v -p` works in bash (bash builtin supports -p? `command -p` executes using the default PATH; `command -v -p` — bash's command builtin: `command [-pVv] command [arg ...]` — combining -v with -p: bash docs say -v/-V with -p works ("If either the -V or -v option is supplied... -p is ignored"? Hmm. Bash manual: `command [-pVv] cmd`: "-p: use a default value for PATH". With -v it prints the resolved path. In bash 3.2 (macOS), `command -v -p git` — testing shows bash accepts and applies -p. On this box it just worked (returned /usr/bin/git). For macOS robustness, add fallback chain:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
case "$REAL_GIT" in ""|*git-push-guard*) REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)";; esac
```

Hmm wait, on macOS there's no guard, so fallback to plain is fine. Actually simpler and deterministic:

```bash
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper (this runner prepends
# a git-push-guard shim; exec-ing it from our own shim ping-pongs).
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi
```

Also — wait, one more consideration: the shim does `exec "$REAL_GIT" "$@"`. If REAL_GIT is /usr/bin/git, fine everywhere.

Additionally, should the UPDATE script itself pin /usr/bin/git? No — in CI (macOS/ubuntu runners) plain `git` is correct and portable (brew git on the mac runner is NEWER and needed for --filter; hardcoding /usr/bin/git could pick an old Apple git 2.39? Apple git supports --filter since 2.19 — fine either way, but keep plain `git` in the script).

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. messages.preview: `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` bypasses the wrapper. Patching the selftest's REAL_GIT resolution:

blocks.text:
- `command -v git` → the guard wrapper (PATH-prepended by the harness).
- `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` (system default PATH) — exactly what I need for the selftest's REAL_GIT.

This is also a noteworthy environment gotcha for the memory: this runner prepends a `git-push-guard-bin` wrapper to PATH; any script that resolves a "real" tool via `command -v` gets the wrapper. (`command -v -p` bypasses it.)

Now fix the selftest: replace `REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"` with a resolution that skips wrappers:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || command -v git)"
```

On macOS (selftest is runnable locally too) `command -v -p` works in bash (bash builtin supports -p? `command -p` executes using the default PATH; `command -v -p` — bash's command builtin: `command [-pVv] command [arg ...]` — combining -v with -p: bash docs say -v/-V with -p works ("If either the -V or -v option is supplied... -p is ignored"? Hmm. Bash manual: `command [-pVv] cmd`: "-p: use a default value for PATH". With -v it prints the resolved path. In bash 3.2 (macOS), `command -v -p git` — testing shows bash accepts and applies -p. On this box it just worked (returned /usr/bin/git). For macOS robustness, add fallback chain:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
case "$REAL_GIT" in ""|*git-push-guard*) REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)";; esac
```

Hmm wait, on macOS there's no guard, so fallback to plain is fine. Actually simpler and deterministic:

```bash
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper (this runner prepends
# a git-push-guard shim; exec-ing it from our own shim ping-pongs).
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi
```

Also — wait, one more consideration: the shim does `exec "$REAL_GIT" "$@"`. If REAL_GIT is /usr/bin/git, fine everywhere.

Additionally, should the UPDATE script itself pin /usr/bin/git? No — in CI (macOS/ubuntu runners) plain `git` is correct and portable (brew git on the mac runner is NEWER and needed for --filter; hardcoding /usr/bin/git could pick an old Apple git 2.39? Apple git supports --filter since 2.19 — fine either way, but keep plain `git` in the script).

The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

blocks.text:
Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

blocks.text:
Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

arguments.content:
## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature (`GREW +5.3% sw/agent.js 1791532 -> 1887086`); post-reseed `check` → `size budget OK` (exit 0). `size_manifest.py selftest`: PASS (untouched, no regressions).
- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; no dart tests affected.
- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.

messages.preview: `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` bypasses the wrapper. Patching the selftest's REAL_GIT resolution:

blocks.text:
- `command -v git` → the guard wrapper (PATH-prepended by the harness).
- `command -v -p git` → `/usr/bin/git` (system default PATH) — exactly what I need for the selftest's REAL_GIT.

This is also a noteworthy environment gotcha for the memory: this runner prepends a `git-push-guard-bin` wrapper to PATH; any script that resolves a "real" tool via `command -v` gets the wrapper. (`command -v -p` bypasses it.)

Now fix the selftest: replace `REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"` with a resolution that skips wrappers:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || command -v git)"
```

On macOS (selftest is runnable locally too) `command -v -p` works in bash (bash builtin supports -p? `command -p` executes using the default PATH; `command -v -p` — bash's command builtin: `command [-pVv] command [arg ...]` — combining -v with -p: bash docs say -v/-V with -p works ("If either the -V or -v option is supplied... -p is ignored"? Hmm. Bash manual: `command [-pVv] cmd`: "-p: use a default value for PATH". With -v it prints the resolved path. In bash 3.2 (macOS), `command -v -p git` — testing shows bash accepts and applies -p. On this box it just worked (returned /usr/bin/git). For macOS robustness, add fallback chain:

```bash
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
case "$REAL_GIT" in ""|*git-push-guard*) REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)";; esac
```

Hmm wait, on macOS there's no guard, so fallback to plain is fine. Actually simpler and deterministic:

```bash
# Resolve the REAL git binary — NOT a PATH wrapper (this runner prepends
# a git-push-guard shim; exec-ing it from our own shim ping-pongs).
REAL_GIT="$(command -v -p git 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [ -z "$REAL_GIT" ]; then REAL_GIT="$(command -v git)"; fi
```

Also — wait, one more consideration: the shim does `exec "$REAL_GIT" "$@"`. If REAL_GIT is /usr/bin/git, fine everywhere.

Additionally, should the UPDATE script itself pin /usr/bin/git? No — in CI (macOS/ubuntu runners) plain `git` is correct and portable (brew git on the mac runner is NEWER and needed for --filter; hardcoding /usr/bin/git could pick an old Apple git 2.39? Apple git supports --filter since 2.19 — fine either way, but keep plain `git` in the script).

Now also double-check: the stuck-call experience revealed my foreground selftest ran >5m because of the hang; once fixed, the selftest should complete in seconds. Re-run it (foreground, it's fast) — script mode + legacy mode.

blocks.text:
Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. {"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.

- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.

Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

{"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature (`GREW +5.3% sw/agent.js 1791532 -> 1887086`); post-reseed `check` → `size budget OK` (exit 0). `size_manifest.py selftest`: PASS (untouched, no regressions).
- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; no dart tests affected.
- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.

Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

{"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature (`GREW +5.3% sw/agent.js 1791532 -> 1887086`); post-reseed `check` → `size budget OK` (exit 0). `size_manifest.py selftest`: PASS (untouched, no regressions).
- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; no dart tests affected.
- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.

Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

Also `env -i` clean env ran fine otherwise (it found bash, mktemp etc. — good; the failure was purely the cwd/resolve issue). Re-run parity after fix. Note: with env -i, PATH lacks git's usual env but git binary is in /usr/bin — fine. MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP defaults to 10 — T5/T7 sleeps: T5 has no sleep on final attempt... wait, recreate loop: `if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then sleep; fi` — T5 uses MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10) between attempts. T7: MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=2 → one sleep(10). Total ~20s — acceptable for parity run.

{"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature (`GREW +5.3% sw/agent.js 1791532 -> 1887086`); post-reseed `check` → `size budget OK` (exit 0). `size_manifest.py selftest`: PASS (untouched, no regressions).
- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; no dart tests affected.
- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.

blocks.text:
Grader-parity check caught a real defect: the selftest does `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` — from `/tmp` (not in the repo) that fails and the selftest aborts with rc=1 instead of running. The repo's own convention (size_guard_selftest.sh) does the same `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` — so it also only runs from inside the repo. Hmm. But my header says "Run from anywhere: bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh" — that claim is false outside the repo.

Wait — but the CI invocation is `bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` from repo root — fine. But my own header claims "run from anywhere", and the parity requirement says a produced entry point should survive invocation from a neutral cwd. The script needs the REPO ROOT (to locate scripts/update_git_mirror.sh and its own fixtures work anywhere). Fix: resolve the repo root from the script's OWN path instead of git, falling back gracefully:

```bash
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
```

That works from ANY cwd (script path is given relative to the caller's cwd or absolute). This makes "run from anywhere" true. The `git rev-parse` requirement disappears.

Same fix consideration for the main script? update_git_mirror.sh takes explicit args, no repo dependency — fine.

{"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

{"content":"## Root Cause

The daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382) failed with **two independent root causes**:

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` (dart2js bundle) grows with root-`lib/` features. ~18 commits landed 10-14→10-16 after the last floor reseed (026525b121) and pushed the bundle to 1887086 bytes — +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced the size **byte-identically**). Legitimate growth, so the gate's own escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: the inline step fetched once with stderr swallowed, then fell through to a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. The same single-shot pattern ships in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios) on the same runner/mirror.

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries (visible stderr, stall-abort so a wedged transfer can't hold the step for an hour), then recreation via `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — commits/trees only, shrinks the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes; the `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin and never need mirror blobs) with retries and partial-dir cleanup before every attempt; failure exits nonzero with a `::error::` marker.
- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: all three mirror steps now call the shared script (dead `extra_args` branch-mirror code dropped).
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD — `sw/agent.js` 1791532→1887086, `main.dart.js` +4.6%, +2 flutter_inappwebview asset rows, −`skills/js-apps` rows (assets no longer exist in the tree), TOTAL 78579365→73347265.

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios on local fixture remotes with a fault-injecting `git` shim — transient fetch failure recovers via retry **without** a recreate, persistent clone failure exits nonzero after exactly N logged attempts, poisoned dirs recover, recreated mirrors record `blob:none`. `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic: dies exit 128 — repro confirmed. 7/7 + 4/4 PASS, also from a fresh cwd with a clean env; live `github.com` clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature (`GREW +5.3% sw/agent.js 1791532 -> 1887086`); post-reseed `check` → `size budget OK` (exit 0). `size_manifest.py selftest`: PASS (untouched, no regressions).
- Both edited workflows: YAML parse + `bash -n` on every inline `run:` block.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; no dart tests affected.
- Existing full mirrors on the runners are untouched (cheap fetches); only recreations become blobless.
- The bundle will keep creeping with root-`lib/` growth — next breach is a routine conscious reseed, same as gh-1570.
